rounds.text: International Conveyors Ltd presents a compelling case of extreme undervaluation, trading at a P/E of 3.62x compared to a sector benchmark of 22.4x [E1, E6]. This valuation disconnect is further highlighted by a price-to-book ratio of 1.16x, significantly lower than the sector benchmark of 2.44x [E2, E7]. The company demonstrates superior capital efficiency, with an ROE of 18.7% and ROCE of 22.0%, both of which comfortably exceed their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E12, E13]. Profit growth has been robust, maintaining a 34% CAGR over the last decade and accelerating to 45% in the trailing twelve months [E17, E18]. Furthermore, the company is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.17x and a strong current ratio of 3.95x [E38, E39]. Conceded: the company has delivered poor sales growth of 4.72% over the past five years, earnings include other income of Rs 140 Cr, and working capital days have increased from 118 to 173 [E63, E64, E65].

The company’s reported earnings quality is highly questionable, as evidenced by the inclusion of Rs 140 Cr in other income [E64]. While headline profit growth appears strong, the cash conversion ratio of 0.51x for March 2026 indicates that reported profits are significantly outpacing actual cash generation [E34]. This discrepancy is further compounded by a deterioration in operational efficiency, with working capital days ballooning from 118 to 173 days [E65]. Stagnant top-line performance remains a structural concern, as evidenced by 0% compounded sales growth over the last three years [E16] and poor five-year sales growth of 4.72% [E63]. Furthermore, institutional investors are actively reducing their exposure, as reflected by negative money flow [E45] and a decline in institutional holdings [E71]. Conceded: [E1], [E8], [E10], [E11], [E38], and [E46] suggest the stock is attractively valued and fundamentally robust by several traditional metrics. Investors should weigh these valuation arguments against the clear evidence of declining institutional confidence and the reliance on non-operating income to bolster the bottom line [E45], [E64].

The bear’s focus on other income [E64] ignores the company’s underlying operational strength, evidenced by a 20% operating margin that has expanded by 4 to 5 percentage points recently [E30, E31]. While the cash conversion ratio of 0.51x is a point of concern [E34], the company still generated Rs 35 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 31 Cr in free cash flow in March 2026 [E35, E36], demonstrating that the business remains a cash-generative entity. Conceded: the increase in working capital days [E65] and the 0% three-year sales growth [E16] represent structural challenges. However, the bear overlooks the recent 45% trailing twelve-month sales growth [E17] and consistent profit growth of 38% over the last three years [E20], which suggest a significant recent turnaround in performance. Furthermore, while institutional money flow is currently negative [E45], the broader institutional participation has actually increased significantly since 2023, with foreign and domestic holdings rising by 0.56 and 0.52 percentage points respectively [E43, E44]. The stock’s valuation remains deeply discounted relative to sector benchmarks [E6, E7, E11], and the current price is supported by both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E51].
